title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
keyIdea: The smallest remaining value is always at the front of one of the two lists. Repeatedly splice the smaller front node after a tail pointer, then attach whatever is left of the other list in one step. Relink existing nodes; don't copy.

approaches.name: Copy into new nodes (first version)
approaches.idea: Same comparisons, but every value is copied into a new ListNode, and both leftovers are copied in loops.
approaches.why: Creates m + n new nodes instead of reusing the existing ones.

approaches.name: Dummy node (Kunal's)
approaches.idea: Start from a fake node so the first splice is like every other; return dummy->next.
approaches.why: Relinks nodes; one extra node for convenience.

approaches.name: Pick the real head first (your better version)
approaches.idea: Handle empty lists, choose the smaller front as head, then splice with temp and attach the rest.
approaches.why: Every node is visited once and relinked, no new nodes at all.

quiz.q: Why can the leftover list be attached with one assignment?
options: It's already sorted and every value in it is ≥ everything merged so far
It can't, it needs a loop

quiz.q: What does a dummy node save you?
options: The special case of choosing the head before the loop

quiz.q: Why is the in-place version O(1) space but the first version O(m + n)?
options: It relinks existing nodes instead of creating new ones
